implemented.cold_generation: compile_plan after successful final prepare_placed_steps, before returning/adopting the exact executable. No generation on failed route candidates.
facts: Sorted unique logical external-input IDs whose actual external root has a non-self direct physical alias child. A descendant necessarily has such a direct child; no lease/address is cached.

Sorted records {logical value, actual physical instance, selected final step, input port} for ALL step inputs whose logical value has kExternalInput. Includes copy steps and other-storage physical replicas, not just uses of external_instances[value].
Root stays in existing external_instances. No descriptor, lease, prepared implementation, per-invocation permission or readiness table is copied.
implemented.lookup: Binary lookup plus only this logical input's consumer records replaces the two whole-Plan scans. Step kind, selected artifact and current requested readers are still checked from the original Plan/runtime.
implemented.finite: Finite-only shell returns before physical placement/index creation. Executable::create_invocation resolves a matched exact variant and delegates; each child goes through ordinary final compile_plan index creation. General symbolic Plan also builds its static selected topology once.
implemented.lifetime: Metadata uses plan.allocator and is declared on PlanState. No mutable global state/executor/hot cache. Its destruction occurs inside normal PlanState destruction while metadata_owner and allocator are still retained.
implemented.allocation_failure: Only try_push_back growth can allocate in the new builder. Any false return reaches existing plan_allocation_failure/release(plan) failure path; no partial executable is published. Existing local CompileReport/constant preparation owners unwind normally.

implemented.unchanged_errors: Alias descendant, foreign reader step, wrong selected artifact/port, duplicate proof, unqualified physical reader, no reader, and foreign native-capacity page messages/order are retained within each strict entry point.

complexity.cold_generation: O(I + P + A log A + C log C), once per selected physical Plan.
complexity.storage: Two zero-inline allocator-owned SmallVectors: O(A + C) capacity, unique logical alias IDs (4 bytes payload each) and four-u32 consumer records (16 bytes payload each), plus vector metadata/capacity slack. No allocation when their payloads are empty.
complexity.limit: This optimizes the identified strict topology scans only. invocation.bind, recording invalidation, page checking and the more general alias-allowing ReadProjection API retain their own existing costs. No end-to-end speed claim.

cold_consumer_equivalence.old_predicate: For the queried logical input L, enumerate every final Plan step/input port and retain those whose plan.instance_values[input]==L.
cold_consumer_equivalence.new_predicate: build_external_input_topology enumerates exactly the same final Plan steps/ports. It stores {value=L, instance=input, step, port} for every logical external input, selecting by logical binding_roles, not physical instance_roles or external-root identity.
cold_consumer_equivalence.replicas_and_transfers: Copy step input_count is1 and it enters this same enumeration. Other-storage replicas retain the original logical instance_values mapping and are therefore included even though their physical instance differs from external_instances[L]. No copy/non-region consumer is silently filtered.
cold_consumer_equivalence.runtime: The binary lookup returns the complete contiguous L group, ordered by step/port. bind_projected_impl still requires every recorded consumer to be the actual external physical root, a Region, and covered by a supplied exact selected-artifact/port proof. projection_resource still restricts it to the exact decoder step and bank port, with original operation/region kinds. Empty consumer groups still reject.
cold_consumer_equivalence.proof_scope: Valid queried L is an actual graph input: find_binding compares full ValueId/generation and the fixed input record, or projection_resource explicitly requires the logical external-input role. Thus filtering the cold table to external logical inputs does not lose any old eligible query.
cold_consumer_equivalence.stability: Construction is called once after prepare_placed_steps succeeds, after physical replica/copy insertion, alias/workspace choices and final step scheduling. Runtime preparation does not mutate those final Plan arrays. Existing build_segments rejects exhausted step identity space before uint32 step storage.

alias_equivalence.old: Reject queried root P=external_instances[L] iff there exists i!=P with alias_sources[i]==P.
alias_equivalence.new: For each nonself alias child i with parent P, record instance_values[P] only if P is exactly that external logical input's external_instances entry. Sort/unique the resulting L values and binary-search L at the old rejection site.
alias_equivalence.iff: The root mapping invariant instance_values[external_instances[L]]==L makes each old direct-child witness insert L; conversely every inserted L names an actual old direct-child witness of its external root. Self aliases are skipped in both versions.
alias_equivalence.descendants: The existing validated physical alias DAG has a finite parent chain. Any descendant chain contains a direct child of P. No new recursive walk or assumptions about logical View aliases are introduced. A direct child of a replica is not mistaken for a child of the external root; replica readers are separately retained by the consumer table.

finite_and_exact.finite_shell: compile_plan finite_shell returns the semantic parent before general physical metadata and before the new build call. Its two zero-inline vectors remain empty and own no payload. projection_resource rejects an unselected shell through its existing absent physical input metadata checks.
finite_and_exact.selected_child: Each actual exact child is independently built by compile_plan(...finite_shell=false), so it gets its own final topology table. create_invocation dispatches a matching finite/exact shape to that child before constructing actual resources or exposing a runnable invocation.
finite_and_exact.declared_domain: A general declared-domain Plan also builds its immutable final topology once. Per-invocation concrete descriptions/bindings do not change the physical step/input/alias topology. No parent table is reused as a child's proof.

OOM_and_cleanup.storage: Both new SmallVector<T,0,AllocatorRef> members use the original Plan allocator, including its metadata owner/compilation-budget wrapper when selected. Records contain only four uint32 values or one uint32 alias value, with no owner/payload references.
OOM_and_cleanup.failure: Every push uses try_push_back and returns plan_allocation_failure on allocation failure. The caller follows its existing !status.ok release(plan) path. A partially filled alias/consumer vector remains owned by the unpublished Plan and is destroyed; no Invocation or external work has been admitted.
OOM_and_cleanup.lifetime: The vectors are declared at the end of PlanState, so their storage is destroyed before the earlier allocator/budget/metadata-owner members. PlanState::destroy retains metadata_owner locally through destructor and deallocation. No new transfer/lease cleanup policy is introduced.
OOM_and_cleanup.nonthrowing_operations: The entries and alias values are trivial; sorting/unique/erase requires no element-owned allocation or throwing user comparator. Empty-table guards avoid null iterator subtraction/sort ranges. The constructor initializes both containers with the same valid allocator.
OOM_and_cleanup.scope_limit: No new explicit index-only OOM test was authored by this reviewer. Root's selected20-case run includes EveryMetadataAllocationFailureIsFatalAndReclaimsPlans, but this source review does not claim that its fault schedule necessarily hits every newly added allocation site.

live_permission_and_failure_contract.not_cached: Neither table contains native addresses, memory resources, tensors, ReadLease/WriteLease, readiness, page bounds, provider invocation state or permissions. The tables are immutable topology facts only.
unchanged_dynamic_checks: Current reader proofs still verify step bounds, actual selected artifact identity, exact input port and physical root. Duplicate supplied physical ports are still rejected.
Empty-footprint inspectors still run against the current actual region invocation when the current bind supplies no pages.
Every actual page view is checked against current tensor resource/native_handle/offset/capacity. Metadata cannot authorize a foreign or missing current page.

Permission capacity and current ordinary Invocation::bind checks precede the unchanged commit. Failed checks preserve prior binding/permissions; successful bind invalidates replay and replaces actual current guards through the original path.
The original result lease, resource episode, completion/retirement and pending-footprint behavior is unchanged.
live_permission_and_failure_contract.other_projection_paths: The general bind_read_projection alias-aware path is unchanged. This is not a new blanket cache of all projection admission or a claim that every binding scan has disappeared.

complexity.cold: Let I=physical instances, E=all final step input ports, C=direct external-root alias witnesses and Eext=ports reading external logical inputs. One cold pass costs O(I+E+C log C+Eext log Eext). Resident vector capacity is O(C+Eext); duplicate alias size is reduced but capacity need not shrink.
complexity.strict_region_bind: The previous O(I+E) whole-Plan scans become O(log U+log Eext+E_L*R), where U=unique aliased input roots, E_L=actual consumer ports of this logical input and R=supplied proofs. Existing O(R^2) duplicate-proof checks, live page validation and fixed resource-episode scans remain.
complexity.row_resource_lookup: Its previous whole-Plan alias/consumer scans become O(log U+log Eext+E_L), in addition to the unchanged selected-access-node inspection and resource checks.
complexity.limit: No measured performance gain or complete O(1) bind claim. No per-bind index allocation or mutation; no hash map or secondary live permission state.

test_review.coverage_limit: The new case directly covers strict region projected bind, not every row decoder/finite variant/OOM path. Existing selected neighbors cover those surrounding contracts to the extent their actual root-run selection states. No unrun coverage is called passed.
